36406110_0c02eb87.text: The intergeniculate leaflet (IGL) of the lateral geniculate body of rodents, a homologue of the pre-geniculate nucleus in primates (Moore, 1989), is a structure known for its role in the regulation of circadian rhythmicity (Morin, 1994))

36406110_2999c838.text: .The most abundant neurotransmitter synthesized by IGL neurons is c-aminobutyric acid (Moore & Speh, 1993). In the majority of IGL neurons, c-aminobutyric acid is co-localized with neuropeptide Y (NPY) or enkephalin. In the rat IGL, a third cell group is present with unknown neurotransmitter content (Moore & Card, 1994). NPY-containing IGL neurons form the geniculo-hypothalamic tract that terminates in the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN), considered to be the main circadian 'pacemaker' in the circadian timing system

36406110_fb6083ff.text: .Identified, neuropeptide Y-positive IGL neurons, known to influence suprachiasmatic nucleus activity, were excited by R3/I5, whereas neurons of unidentified neurotransmitter content were either depolarized or displayed a decrease in action potential firing and/or membrane potential hyperpolarization.
